items.title: Tweedie identity, positive Jacobian, and the MMSE proximal potential
items.statement:
Let $n\ge1$, let $\mu$ be a Borel probability measure on $\mathbb R^n$ that is not concentrated on any affine hyperplane, and let $\sigma,\gamma>0$. Put
$$\rho_\sigma(w)=\exp\!\left(-\frac{\|w\|_2^2}{2\sigma^2}\right),\qquad p_\sigma(z)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}\rho_\sigma(z-u)\,\mu(du),$$
and define the normalized posterior measure and its mean by
$$\nu_{\sigma,z}(E)=\frac{\int_E\rho_\sigma(z-u)\,\mu(du)}{p_\sigma(z)}\quad(E\in\mathcal B(\mathbb R^n)),\qquad D_\sigma(z)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}u\,\nu_{\sigma,z}(du).$$
The omitted normalizing constant of the $N(0,\sigma^2I)$ likelihood is independent of $u$ and cancels in $\nu_{\sigma,z}$. Writing $U(u)=u$ for the identity random vector under $\nu_{\sigma,z}$, its covariance matrix is
$$\operatorname{Cov}_{\nu_{\sigma,z}}(U)=\int_{\mathbb R^n}(u-D_\sigma(z))(u-D_\sigma(z))^{\mathsf T}\,\nu_{\sigma,z}(du).$$
Then $p_\sigma$ is positive and smooth, each $\nu_{\sigma,z}$ has finite second moment, and $D_\sigma(z)$ uniquely minimizes the posterior squared-error risk $a\mapsto\int\|u-a\|_2^2\,\nu_{\sigma,z}(du)$. Moreover, $D_\sigma$ is smooth and
$$J D_\sigma(z)=\sigma^{-2}\operatorname{Cov}_{\nu_{\sigma,z}}(U)$$
is symmetric positive definite. Hence $D_\sigma$ is injective with open image $X_\sigma=D_\sigma(\mathbb R^n)$ and smooth inverse on $X_\sigma$. Put $q_\sigma=-\log p_\sigma$ and, for $x\in X_\sigma$, define
$$h_{\sigma,\gamma}(x)=-\frac{\|x-D_\sigma^{-1}(x)\|_2^2}{2\gamma}+\frac{\sigma^2}{\gamma}q_\sigma(D_\sigma^{-1}(x));$$
set $h_{\sigma,\gamma}(x)=+\infty$ outside $X_\sigma$. The restriction of $h_{\sigma,\gamma}$ to $X_\sigma$ is smooth. For any extended-real $h:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$, define
$$\operatorname{prox}^{\mathrm{glob}}_{\gamma h}(z)=\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\left\{\frac12\|x-z\|_2^2+\gamma h(x)\right\},$$
where the argmin is the set of global minimizers and $h$ need not be convex. Then
$$D_\sigma(z)=z+\sigma^2\nabla\log p_\sigma(z)=z-\sigma^2\nabla q_\sigma(z),\qquad \operatorname{prox}^{\mathrm{glob}}_{\gamma h_{\sigma,\gamma}}(z)=\{D_\sigma(z)\}\quad(z\in\mathbb R^n).$$

references.title: Xiaojian Xu, Yu Sun, Jiaming Liu, Brendt Wohlberg, and Ulugbek S. Kamilov, Provable Convergence of Plug-and-Play Priors with MMSE Denoisers, IEEE Signal Processing Letters 27 (2020), arXiv:2005.07685

items.title: Exact-MMSE PnP-ISTA has monotone objective and vanishing gradient
items.statement:
Let $n\ge1$, let $\sigma>0$, and let $\mu$ be a Borel probability measure on $\mathbb R^n$ that is not concentrated on any affine hyperplane. Use the analytic Gaussian posterior-mean map $D_\sigma$ and potential $h_{\sigma,\gamma}$ constructed from $\mu$ in the local lemma. items.title: An arbitrary denoiser does not inherit the exact-MMSE objective
items.statement: For $\gamma>0$, a global proximal selection of an extended-real penalty $h:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$ is a map $P:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ such that, for every $z\in\mathbb R$, $P(z)$ is a global minimizer of $x\mapsto\frac12|x-z|^2+\gamma h(x)$. The potential $h_{\sigma,\gamma}$ in the exact-MMSE stationarity result is constructed from the conditional-mean map $D_\sigma$. Replacing $D_\sigma$ in PnP-ISTA by an arbitrary map $\widetilde D_\sigma$ does not in general give a global proximal representation or inherit that stationarity conclusion: for every $\gamma>0$, the map $z\mapsto-z$ is not a global proximal selection of any such $h$ that is finite somewhere and nowhere $-\infty$. This does not assert that a particular other denoiser has no different objective.

title: Plug-and-play MMSE denoisers and stationarity — Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: Exact scalar MMSE denoiser for a two-point prior
items.statement:
Let $a,\sigma,\gamma>0$ and let the scalar prior put mass $1/2$ at each of $-a$ and $a$. Under the Gaussian likelihood kernel $\rho_\sigma(z-u)=\exp(-(z-u)^2/(2\sigma^2))$, its exact posterior-mean map is
$$D_\sigma(z)=a\tanh\!\left(\frac{az}{\sigma^2}\right),\qquad \tanh(s)=\frac{\exp(s)-\exp(-s)}{\exp(s)+\exp(-s)}.$$
The normalizing constant of the Gaussian likelihood cancels in the posterior. For every $z$, $D_\sigma(z)$ uniquely minimizes the posterior squared-error risk and, with the potential $h_{\sigma,\gamma}$ constructed from this prior, is the unique global minimizer of $x\mapsto (x-z)^2/2+\gamma h_{\sigma,\gamma}(x)$.

references.locator: Appendix A.1, equation (7) and equations (9)–(12); the finite two-point posterior weights are computed locally.

items.title: Gaussian measurement noise need not remain Gaussian at later PnP-ISTA inputs
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\varepsilon$ have the standard normal law, let $Y=\theta+\varepsilon$, and let $g(x)=(x-Y)^2/2$. For any noise parameter $\sigma>0$, deterministic map $\widetilde D_\sigma:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, step $\gamma>0$, and initialization $x_0\in\mathbb R$, define $z_t=x_{t-1}-\gamma(x_{t-1}-Y)$ and $x_t=\widetilde D_\sigma(z_t)$. The false claim is that Gaussian measurement noise forces $z_t-\theta$ to have a Gaussian law at every iteration $t\ge1$, for every such denoiser, step, and initialization.

items.title: A biased one-pixel CNN approximates but is not the exact MMSE denoiser
items.statement:
Let $a,\sigma>0$ and use the scalar two-point prior assigning mass $1/2$ to each of $-a$ and $a$, whose exact Gaussian posterior-mean map is $D_\sigma(z)=a\tanh(az/\sigma^2)$, where $\tanh(s)=(\exp(s)-\exp(-s))/(\exp(s)+\exp(-s))$. For any tolerance $\eta>0$, choose $b$ with $0<|b|<\eta$ and define the one-pixel convolutional neural network (CNN) map
$$\widetilde D_\sigma(z)=a\tanh(az/\sigma^2)+b.$$
This map is implemented by a $1\times1$ convolution, a $\tanh$ activation, output scaling, and an output bias $b$. It satisfies $\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}|\widetilde D_\sigma(z)-D_\sigma(z)|=|b|<\eta$, while $\widetilde D_\sigma(0)\ne D_\sigma(0)$. It is approximate and does not meet the exact-denoiser hypothesis of the stationarity theorem; this example makes no claim that it lacks some other objective.
